title: Robotics startup Generalist reaches $3B valuation with AI foundation model for robots
summary: Generalist, a robotics startup founded by former Google DeepMind researchers and a Boston Dynamics engineer, has raised $200 million in additional funding, bringing its total Series B round to $600 million and its valuation to $3 billion. The company is developing an AI foundation model that enables robots to learn new tasks from short video demonstrations (3-12 seconds). Generalist operates with select customers to refine its Gen 1.5 model for specific use cases, competing in a growing market alongside startups like Physical Intelligence and Skild AI. Investors are betting on a potential 'ChatGPT moment' for robotics, though challenges remain in training general-purpose robotic models.
key_points: Generalist, a robotics startup, has reached a $3 billion valuation after raising $200 million in additional funding, extending its $400 million Series B round to $600 million.

Founded in 2024 by former Google DeepMind researchers Pete Florence and Andy Zeng, and ex-Boston Dynamics engineer Andrew Barry, the startup has backing from 8VC, Radical Ventures, Nvidia, and others.
Generalist is developing an AI foundation model (Gen 1.5) that allows robots to learn new tasks from 3-12 second video demonstrations.
The company works with a limited set of customers to tailor its model for specific use cases, operating with minimal publicity until recently.
Competitors in the space include Physical Intelligence ($11B valuation), Skild AI ($14B valuation), and Genesis AI (in talks for a $3B valuation).
Investors are optimistic about a 'ChatGPT moment' for robotics, though some VCs caution that general-purpose robotic models may still be years away due to training limitations.
